statusText: CME equity futures are halted for fourteen of the twenty-four published hours, holding Tail at the floor of a closed venue. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window, leaving the 22:00Z Sunday restart as the only slot carrying materially elevated conditional risk. Nothing new was verified in the hour since the previous assessment, so the escalation-versus-supply-repair balance is carried forward unchanged.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 5 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is published at Tail 18, still inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: A quiet hour on a shut venue: every primary mark re-verified unchanged, no new Middle East escalation confirmed, and the balance between a ten-country embassy alert perimeter and six-month-high Hormuz throughput carried forward intact into the 22:00Z restart
body:
Fourteen of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final ten contain the 22:00Z restart, the hour after it and the Asian session that follows. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since 21:00Z that day. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run and every one is unchanged: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08% from 15.44 inside a 14.80-15.63 day range and near the lower end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range. Crude settled easier for a third consecutive session, WTI at 100.30 and Brent at 103.87, although WTI remains up about 18.85% over the month because the East-West pipeline has been offline since the 11 September strike.

The defining feature of this run is that nothing material changed in the hour since the previous assessment. A deliberate re-check of the weekend record found no new escalation and no new damage assessment. The picture therefore stands as before, and it remains two-sided. On the escalatory side, US embassies in ten Middle East countries - Bahrain, Israel, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE - issued alerts warning that the conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly and flagging possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and travel disruption. Those alerts follow Saturday's two claimed Houthi operations against sensitive sites in Riyadh and Aramco facilities at Yanbu. On the de-escalatory side, the verified outcome record is unchanged: the coalition says the ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh was intercepted and destroyed, Saudi authorities report no casualties or damage, and the fuel-depot fire near King Khalid International Airport was extinguished, although FlightRadar24 recorded a maximum disruption reading at that airport. The supply evidence continues to point the other way from the alerts: US Central Command reports Hormuz crude and LNG throughput over the past fortnight at a six-month high, and reporting on Friday's easier crude tape attributed the weekly loss to fading Saudi export fears. A weekend that is escalatory and de-escalatory at once remains the classic setup for two-way price discovery at the reopen rather than a persistent one-way path, and under the risk definition used here conflicting evidence lifts Stress ahead of Tail.

The macro backdrop is restrictive and was re-verified in more detail this run. The FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first increase since 2023, on a 12-0 vote. The accompanying projections were hawkish: the median 2026 dot at 4.1% implies one further 25 basis point increase this year, with sixteen of eighteen participants expecting at least one more and four seeing two. The H.15 release dated 18 September shows the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the 30-year at 5.29% as of 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%. That backdrop is the persistent named driver carried across the published hours, and a yield extension during Asian trade is the cross-asset condition most likely to slow the Tail decay published after the restart.

Two index-level checkpoints sit just outside the window. The Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance is confirmed and takes effect at Monday's cash open, lifting SpaceX from a weight of about 1.28% to 2.82% after its free float was recalculated on Friday's close, which helps explain the heavy and uneven quarterly triple-witching expiry. More than 200 products tracking the benchmark, with over $800bn in assets including the $482bn Invesco QQQ Trust, must adjust. Separately, a Trump-Xi meeting has been reported for around 24 September alongside the UN General Assembly, but Beijing has not confirmed it; because the timing is materially uncertain it is omitted from the published calendar rather than guessed, and is carried only as an unconfirmed checkpoint. Neither item is a path variable for the hours published here, and mechanical rebalancing turnover is not the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures.

Friday's tape supports carrying no structural amplifier forward. The session was rotational rather than uniform - the Nasdaq added 0.7% while the Dow closed about 95 points lower and the S&P 500 rose 0.2%. Latest-session internals corroborate that split: four of the eight Nasdaq megacaps closed higher and four lower, with a mean change near +0.24%, while semiconductors led at roughly +1.28% mean, with QCOM an outlier at -5.82%, and both software industry groups closed lower. That shared context is delayed latest-session data and is used here only as confirmation, never as live NQ price evidence; its futures and calendar sections were unavailable this run.

Current Tail stays at the closed-venue floor of 5: no venue is open and no structure has been observed. Stress is published at 30, unchanged, because neither side of the geopolitical ledger moved. Confidence is published at 74, also unchanged: the additional verified FOMC detail and the completed re-verification of every primary mark offset one more hour of distance from the Friday tape and the two unavailable shared-context sections. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the published 24 hours. Tokyo cash equities open at 00:00Z and provide the first regional cash reference since Friday; the China loan prime rate hold has already resolved, matching every forecast in the Reuters survey. The first Monday catalyst, the Goolsbee remarks at 10:30Z, sits beyond the end of the window, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail is published at 5 through the early halt, drifting up in single steps that track time-to-restart rather than observed structure, reaching a window high of 18 at the restart before easing through the Asian session. Every published hour stays inside the low Tail band and the EA_ON mapping, and no danger window is identified.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first fourteen slots, eased to 4 from 22:00Z Saturday through 04:00Z Sunday and returned to 5 across the final three slots. Stress opened at 21, drifted through 22, 23 and 24 across the Saturday afternoon and evening, stepped to 26 shortly after midnight, eased to 25 and then jumped to 29 at 05:00Z as the weekend escalation headlines landed, settling at 28 and then 30 in the closing hours. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence started at 78, decayed to a 72 trough at 21:00Z as distance from the Friday tape grew, then recovered into the mid-70s as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Fourteen of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final ten contain the 22:00Z restart and the Asian hours after it. Cash closed Friday and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday, 18:00 ET. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window; the next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, beyond its end, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 for the current hour, then steps to 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 across the European and early U.S. afternoon before rising one point per hour to a pre-restart 15 at 21:00Z. It reaches the window high of 18 across the 22:00Z restart, eases to 17 for the first full hour and then decays through 15, 14, 13, 12 and 11 before flattening at 10 for the final three hours. That drift tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure and stays inside the low band and the EA_ON mapping in every published hour. Mode is published as event/whipsaw for the restart and the hour after it, then mixed for the first three Asian hours, reflecting expected two-way discovery against a weekend that produced escalation of intent and supply repair at the same time; it returns to normal for the final five hours on the base case that repricing has cleared. The Nasdaq-100 rebalance effective at Monday's cash open sits beyond the window and is carried as a checkpoint, not an amplifier.
